sentences.en: When shall we three meet again in thunder, lightning or in rain?
sentences.zh: 我们在哪里再度会合？是在雷鸣、闪电还是雨中？

sentences.en: Some of the most famous words ever written by Shakespeare and they're spoken, of course, by one of the witches in Macbeth.
sentences.zh: 这是莎士比亚写下的最著名的字句之一，当然，它们出自《麦克白》中的一位女巫之口。

sentences.en: And witches and witchcraft, these are the theme of today's episode of The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 而女巫与巫术，正是今天这期《历史其余部分》的主题。

sentences.en: But wait, before we go any further, by the pricking of my thumbs, something wicked this way comes.
sentences.zh: 但等等，在我们继续之前，“我的大拇指在刺痛，必有邪恶之事临近”。

sentences.en: Dominic Sandbrook, how are you doing?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克·桑德布鲁克，你好吗？

sentences.en: Sledgehammer wit, Tom, as ever.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，一如既往的重锤般犀利风趣。

sentences.en: I'm very well, thank you indeed.
sentences.zh: 我很好，非常谢谢你。

sentences.en: The rapier shark slash.
sentences.zh: 快剑一般的凌厉切割。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, a fan of the dark arts?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，你是黑魔法的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: A practitioner, perhaps?
sentences.zh: 或许是个实践者？

sentences.en: I've got a lot of dark arts stuff in my house because my son is massively into J.K.
sentences.zh: 我家里有很多黑魔法相关的东西，因为我儿子极度迷恋J.K.

sentences.en: Rowling.
sentences.zh: 罗琳。

sentences.en: I know J.K.
sentences.zh: 我知道J.K.

sentences.en: Rowling is persona non grata in some quarters, but this is definitely a Rowling-friendly household.
sentences.zh: 罗琳在某些圈子里不受欢迎，但这里绝对是一个对罗琳友好的家庭。

sentences.en: So my house is stuffed with witchcraft and wizardry and all that sort of carry-on.
sentences.zh: 所以我的屋子里塞满了巫术、魔法以及所有诸如此类的玩意儿。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, that should give us something to talk about.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这应该能给我们提供不少谈资了。

sentences.en: It'd be good, perhaps, to get on to Harry Potter at some point in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 在这个播客的某个时候，能聊到哈利·波特或许是个不错的选择。

sentences.en: But we're very honoured to be joined today by our special guest, Susanna Lipscomb, star of TV, who also happens to be Professor of History at Roehampton University,
sentences.zh: 但今天我们非常荣幸地请到了特别嘉宾苏珊娜·利普斯孔姆，她是一位电视明星，同时也是罗汉普顿大学的历史学教授，

sentences.en: the author of a series of award-winning books on early modern history, including, most recently, The Voices of Neem, about women, sex and marriage in Reformation Languedoc.
sentences.zh: 她是一系列关于近代早期历史的获奖书籍的作者，其中包括最近出版的《尼姆之声》，讲述了宗教改革时期朗格多克的女性、性与婚姻。

sentences.en: But she's also the author, more germanely for our purposes, of the recently published Lady Bird Book of Witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 但对我们而言更切题的是，她也是近期出版的《伯德图书巫术简史》的作者。

sentences.en: Susie, so good to have you.
sentences.zh: 苏茜，很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: Great title.
sentences.zh: 好棒的书名。

sentences.en: Yes, we've moved on slightly from Jack and Jill with Witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们比带着巫术的杰克和吉尔稍微往前迈进了一点。

sentences.en: Well, it's a great series.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个很棒的系列。

sentences.en: I've also written one, so I know that it's the very highest quality scholarship.
sentences.zh: 我也写过一本，所以我知道这是最高水准的学术研究。

sentences.en: And Witchcraft, was this a subject that you kind of got into on the back of your interest in early modern history, or was it the other way around?
sentences.zh: 那么《巫术》这本书，你是由于对近代早期历史的兴趣才涉足这个主题，还是反过来呢？

sentences.en: It's sort of the other way around, because my supervisor, my doctorate, was Robin Briggs,
sentences.zh: 有点像反过来，因为我的博士生导师是罗宾·布里格斯，

sentences.en: who's a great scholar of witchcraft, looked at the witches, the trials of witches in Lorraine,
sentences.zh: 他是研究巫术的伟大学者，主要研究了洛林的女巫和女巫审判，

sentences.en: particularly, which is one of the independent duchies that was particularly keen on executing witches.
sentences.zh: 洛林是那些特别热衷于处决女巫的独立公国之一。

sentences.en: And my college advisor was Lyndall Roper, who's worked on witchcraft and the witch craze in Germany.
sentences.zh: 我的大学导师是林达·罗珀，她研究过德国的巫术和狂热的女巫迷信。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I barely evaded witchcraft, frankly, as my personal studies.
sentences.zh: 所以我的意思是，坦白说，我的个人研究几乎就是险险避开了巫术。

sentences.en: So it's sort of not surprising at all that I've come round to it in the end.
sentences.zh: 因此，我最终绕回这个主题其实一点也不令人意外。

sentences.en: So there's so much to get into.
sentences.zh: 有太多内容可以探讨了。

sentences.en: And I guess the big question, Susie, is, is witchcraft a kind of constant in human history?
sentences.zh: 我想最大的问题是，苏茜，巫术是人类历史中的一种常态吗？

sentences.en: Have we always believed in witches?
sentences.zh: 我们一直都相信女巫的存在吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm guessing you'll say kind of yes and no, will you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜你的回答会是亦正亦邪，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, we have always believed in witches, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，看起来我们一直都相信女巫的存在。

sentences.en: So the earliest case that I've come across is, and this is far more Tom's territory than mine, is ancient Greece.
sentences.zh: 我遇到的最早的案例——这其实比我的领域更接近汤姆的专业——是古希腊。

sentences.en: So it's about 330 BC.
sentences.zh: 大约在公元前330年左右。

sentences.en: There was an alleged witch called Theoros of Lemnos.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个被指控为女巫的人叫利姆诺斯的西奥罗斯。

sentences.en: And so she was prosecuted for casting incantations and using harmful drugs.
sentences.zh: 她因施展咒语和使用有害药物而被起诉。

sentences.en: And then we see it appear again and again throughout time.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看到它在岁月中不断重现。

sentences.en: Basically, time is punctuated by there being witchcraft cases, whether you're talking 30 BC or, you know, just after the, you know, AD BC, or don't call it anymore anymore,
sentences.zh: 基本上，历史是由一个个巫术案件所点缀的，无论你说的是公元前30年，还是，你知道的，刚好在公元前后的交界，或者已经不再这么叫了，

sentences.en: but you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 但你懂我的意思。

sentences.en: But just the end of the modern era.
sentences.zh: 总之就是现代的起点刚刚结束。

sentences.en: And we see this throughout the Anglo-Saxons, we see it in medieval period.
sentences.zh: 我们在盎格鲁-撒克逊时期能看到这一点，在中世纪也能看到。

sentences.en: And so the period I've particularly worked on is where those beliefs become prosecutions, where there's a particularly serious craze, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我特别研究的时期是那些信仰转化为起诉的阶段，也就是我认为出现真正严重狂热的时期。

sentences.en: And people are concerned with trying to persecute witches under law and then have them executed.
sentences.zh: 当时的人们热衷于根据法律迫害女巫并将她们处决。

sentences.en: But they've been with us throughout time.
sentences.zh: 但它们一直伴随着我们贯穿历史。

sentences.en: So is the big shift from thinking witchcraft was fine and it was just something that people did, it might be a bit weird,
sentences.zh: 那么，最大的转变是从认为巫术没问题、只是人们的一种寻常举动——虽然可能有点古怪，

sentences.en: but it was kind of carrying on to thinking that it was sinful and must be extirpated at all costs?
sentences.zh: 但它不过是日常生活的一部分——转变为认为它是罪恶的、必须不惜一切代价铲除的吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it was ever thought to be fine.
sentences.zh: 我不认为人们曾经觉得它没问题。

sentences.en: I think it was always thought to be transgressive.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们一直觉得它是越轨的。

sentences.en: But I think the shift is towards seeing it, I suppose, as not just doing something harmful, but that being infused with a diabolic intent, that a pact has been made with the devil,
sentences.zh: 但我认为转变在于将其视为——不仅仅是做了一件有害的事情，而是其中融入了魔鬼的意图，即与魔鬼达成了某种契约，

sentences.en: so that it is a form of heresy.
sentences.zh: 从而使之成为了一种异端邪说。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think that's the shift.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是转变所在。

sentences.en: Yeah, because I was wondering about heresy, because famously the Middle Ages, described by R.A.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我在想关于异端的问题，中世纪曾被R.A.

sentences.en: Moore as a persecuting society.
sentences.zh: 摩尔著名地描述为一个迫害性的社会。

sentences.en: And the definite sense you get with heresy, and Dominic, we talked about this in relation to the supposed Cathars.
sentences.zh: 对于异端，你绝对能感受到那种意味，多米尼克，我们在讨论所谓的卡特里派时就探讨过这一点。

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们确实探讨过。

sentences.en: It's that you get kind of friars, learned scholars who go back to classical antiquity and kind of plunder it for source material.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就像是有一群修士或博学的学者，他们回溯到古典古代，并在其中搜寻源材料。

sentences.en: And then they kind of create a package and then they project it onto people and it kind of catches fire.
sentences.zh: 然后他们将之打包整合，再强加给人们，接着它就像烈火一样蔓延开来。

sentences.en: And I guess the, is what happens with witchcraft that essentially, what is it, it's by the kind of the 14th century and then really into the 15th century,
sentences.zh: 我想，关于巫术的情况是不是基本上——大概在14世纪到15世纪深入发展时，

sentences.en: that the church starts to conflate sorcery with heresy.
sentences.zh: 教会开始将巫术与异端邪说混为一谈？

sentences.en: And so the assumption becomes that if you were having dealings with the devil, then in a sense you are no longer Christian and therefore you must be targeted for that reason.
sentences.zh: 因此人们的假设变成了：如果你与魔鬼有来往，那么从某种意义上讲你就不再是基督徒，因此你必须因此成为被打击的目标。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's the end of the 15th century and it particularly happens through the famous book Malleus Maleficarum, The Hammer of the Witches,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在15世纪末，特别是通过那本著名的书《女巫之锤》，

sentences.en: which was written by a German Dominican monk called Heinrich Kramer.
sentences.zh: 它是由一个名叫海因里希·克雷默的德国多明尼加修士写的。

sentences.en: And he reproduced a papal bull that had recently been published that said that witches were heretics.
sentences.zh: 他在书中转载了一份刚刚发表的教皇诏书，其中声称女巫就是异端。

sentences.en: So it's exactly that that's happening in terms of elevating the threat of witchcraft from being a local sorcerer to being something that is on a kind of this transcendental level where,
sentences.zh: 所以，正是这种将巫术的威胁从地方性的巫术提升到一种超验层面的转变正在发生，在这里，

sentences.en: you know, there's, you know, this absolute threat to souls as well as life, lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不仅对生命构成了绝对威胁，对灵魂也是绝对的威胁。

sentences.en: And so I think that's crucial.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点至关重要。

sentences.en: And then the other shift that happens is that once that has the weight of the church or supposed weight of the church behind it,
sentences.zh: 随之发生的另一个转变是，一旦它有了教会的支持或据称是教会的支持作为后盾，

sentences.en: then we see it starting to be accepted at an elite level.
sentences.zh: 我们便看到它开始在精英阶层中被接受。

sentences.en: And indeed, we even get demonologies written by members of the elites, including a reigning monarch.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们甚至看到精英阶层（包括在位的君主）的成员也开始撰写魔鬼学著作。

sentences.en: And we end up with seeing it becoming a crime under law.
sentences.zh: 最终我们看到它根据法律成了一种罪行。

sentences.en: So there's kind of two shifts.
sentences.zh: 所以这里大约有两种转变。

sentences.en: So it's become seen as heresy and then become seen as a crime.
sentences.zh: 它先是被视为异端，然后被视为一种罪行。

sentences.en: And that's a crucial thing that has to happen in the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 这是在16世纪必须发生的一个关键变化。

sentences.en: And why does it happen where it does?
sentences.zh: 为什么它恰恰在这些地方发生？

sentences.en: So obviously, Germany is, you mentioned Linda Roper, and she wrote that great book about witchcraft in Germany.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，德国是——你提到了林达·罗珀，她写过那本关于德国巫术的出色著作。

sentences.en: And in England, we think of it as, you know, the Witchfinder General, Matthew Hopkins, and we obviously witchcraft in Scotland, and then the American colonies,
sentences.zh: 而在英格兰，我们会想到诸如“女巫审判长”马修·霍普金斯，当然我们也会想到苏格兰的巫术，以及美洲殖民地，

sentences.en: the crucible and all that kind of carry on.
sentences.zh: 《萨勒姆的女巫》和所有这些纷繁的事物。

sentences.en: But I'm not aware that it's such a big deal in, you know, Spain or Italy or something.
sentences.zh: 但我并不觉得它在西班牙或意大利等地是一件多么了不起的大事。

sentences.en: Is it places where, I mean, to a sort of layman, it would look like it's places with a lot of Protestants.
sentences.zh: 这是不是发生在那些——对门外汉来说，看起来有很多新教徒的地方？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: It certainly does happen in places with a lot of Protestants.
sentences.zh: 它确实往往发生在有很多新教徒的地方。

sentences.en: And I think it helps, as it were, I think in areas where there's a particularly kind of hot form of Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 我认为这有助益，具体而言，我认为在那些存在某种狂热形式的新教的地区，情况更是如此。

sentences.en: So in England, it becomes to be called Puritanism.
sentences.zh: 所以在英格兰，它后来被称为清教主义。

sentences.en: It means that people have a kind of piebald mentality.
sentences.zh: 这意味着人们有一种非黑即白的僵化心态。

sentences.en: They see the world in black and white.
sentences.zh: 他们把世界看成只有黑与白。

sentences.en: They see the devil at work everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们看到魔鬼在无处不在地作祟。

sentences.en: And it's certainly true that in areas like Scotland, in East Anglia and Essex, there and in parts of Germany, we are we do have a particularly sort of inflamed, no pun intended,
sentences.zh: 而且确实在苏格兰、东盎格利亚、埃塞克斯以及德国的部分地区，我们确实拥有某种特别激进的——双关语无意，

sentences.en: culture around Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 围绕新教的文化。

sentences.en: And so that is true.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点确实如此。

sentences.en: But there are trials, although there are fewer, there are trials in Catholic areas.
sentences.zh: 但也有审判发生，尽管数量较少，天主教地区也有审判。

sentences.en: So, for example, I mentioned Lorraine, the Duchy of Lorraine, which is which is broadly Catholic.
sentences.zh: 例如，我提到的洛林，洛林公国，它基本上是一个天主教地区。

sentences.en: And there are there are many trials there.
sentences.zh: 那里也有许多审判。

sentences.en: There aren't that many in France, about 3000 over the period, which is not that many, but there are some in Spain.
sentences.zh: 法国的审判其实没那么多，在此期间大约有3000起，不算太多，但西班牙确实有一些。

sentences.en: So there are trials in Catholic areas.
sentences.zh: 所以在天主教地区也有审判。

sentences.en: It's not quite so clear cut as just being Protestant.
sentences.zh: 它并不完全像仅仅是新教那么泾渭分明。

sentences.en: And I think it's because in this period, whether you're Protestant or Catholic, you're concerned about what is wrong in terms of faith.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为在这个时期，无论你是新教徒还是天主教徒，你都对信仰中出现的问题感到担忧。

sentences.en: The Reformation has produced this kind of atmosphere of angst about the end days, about whether the devil is at work.
sentences.zh: 宗教改革产生了一种对末日、对魔鬼是否在作祟的焦虑氛围。

sentences.en: Perhaps it's slightly more the case amongst Protestants, but Catholics are certainly concerned about it as well.
sentences.zh: 或许在新教徒当中这种情愫稍微多了一点，但天主教徒对此也同样担忧。

sentences.en: Well, Susie, there's a brilliant comment by Carlos Eyre who says that that hunting witches was actually the most intensely ecumenical event of the Reformation era,
sentences.zh: 苏茜，卡洛斯·埃尔有一段精彩的评论，他说搜捕女巫实际上是宗教改革时代最具普世性的事件，

sentences.en: which is a kind of sober way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种比较清醒的说法。

sentences.en: And he kind of talks about, you know, it's almost one of the few aspects of theology where Catholics are reading Protestants and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 他谈到，这几乎是神学中为数不多的几个方面，天主教徒在阅读新教徒的著作，反之亦然。

sentences.en: And I was wondering, I mean, essentially the kind of the real peak of the witchcraft craze is the latter half of the 16th century, moving into the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 我在想，本质上，巫术狂热的真正顶峰出现在16世纪后期并延续到17世纪。

sentences.en: And that's also when confessional identities among Protestants and among Catholics in the wake of the counter-Reformation are really intensifying.
sentences.zh: 这也是反宗教改革之后，新教徒和天主教徒之间的宗派认同真正加剧的时期。

sentences.en: And again, a kind of a counter-effect to that is that you start to get warfare between them, religious war.
sentences.zh: 而作为一种连锁反应，他们之间开始爆发战争，即宗教战争。

sentences.en: Is there a link between the prevalence of witchcraft, the growth,
sentences.zh: 巫术的盛行、发展，

sentences.en: the anxiety about witchcraft and the sense that presumably both Catholics and Protestants have when they're going to war,
sentences.zh: 对巫术的焦虑，以及天主教徒和新教徒在参战时所隐约感受到的，

sentences.en: that they're engaged in some kind of cosmic battle between good and evil?
sentences.zh: 他们正参与某种善恶之间的宇宙大战的感觉，这三者之间是否存在某种联系？

sentences.en: There certainly is.
sentences.zh: 确实存在。

sentences.en: There certainly is.
sentences.zh: 确实存在。

sentences.en: There certainly is this connection that actually they're living in a time of anarchy, spiritual anarchy.
sentences.zh: 确实存在这样一种联系：实际上他们生活在一个无政府状态的时代，精神上的无政府状态。

sentences.en: And, you know, pretty much no one in the 16th century and early 17th century thinks that toleration is a good idea.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在16世纪和17世纪初，几乎没有人认为宽容是个好主意。

sentences.en: You know, they think there is a right way and there's a wrong way and you need to root out that which is wrong.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们认为存在一条正确的道路和一条错误的道路，你需要根除错误的东西。

sentences.en: So it's certainly that's the background to it.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是其中的背景。

sentences.en: I think we have to be careful that it's quite just to prevent against thinking this is Protestants attacking Catholics.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须谨慎，不要简单地认为这是新教徒在攻击天主教徒。

sentences.en: Very few instances where that's the case or vice versa.
sentences.zh: 这种情况或反之的情况非常罕见。

sentences.en: But generally speaking, it's that as that lovely quote makes clear,
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，正如那段优美的引言所阐明的，

sentences.en: it's something that everybody's doing at the time that witches are thought to be a threat overall because people are much more concerned about evil at work in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是当时每个人都在做的事情，人们认为女巫全面构成了威胁，因为人们更关心恶魔在世界上发挥的作用。

sentences.en: They differ on their definition of which particular version of faith is correct, but they do think there's a right in the wrong way and witches are clearly on the wrong side.
sentences.zh: 他们对哪一种具体的信仰版本才是正确的看法不一，但他们确实认为存在正邪之分，而女巫显然站在了错误的一边。

sentences.en: Susie, let's talk a bit about witches themselves.
sentences.zh: 苏茜，我们来谈谈女巫本身吧。

sentences.en: So the sort of standard view of the witches, I guess, is that they are women, older women, childless widows who are marginal in their village.
sentences.zh: 我想，关于女巫的某种标准看法是，她们是女性，年长的女性，在村子里处于边缘地位的无子寡妇。

sentences.en: And it tends to be villages, right, rather than big towns.
sentences.zh: 而且往往是在村子里，对吧，而不是大城镇。

sentences.en: And is that right or is it more complicated than that?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗，还是说情况更复杂？

sentences.en: I mean, do you ever get a male witch, for example?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比方说，你曾经见过男巫吗？

sentences.en: So there's a lot to unpack there.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多细节需要剖析。

sentences.en: So, yes, it tends to be villages rather than towns because most people live in villages, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，往往是村庄而不是城镇，因为大多数人就住在村子里，对吧？

sentences.en: So you don't have that many, like 95% of the population or more lives in villages and small places under 400 people.
sentences.zh: 所以你没有那么多——比如95%甚至更多的人口都住在村庄和400人以下的小地方。

sentences.en: And it's true that most witches that are convicted are women and they're older women.
sentences.zh: 而且确实大多数被定罪的女巫都是女性，而且是年长的女性。

sentences.en: Crucially, they're menopausal or postmenopausal.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，她们处于绝经期或绝经后。

sentences.en: They are often widowed.
sentences.zh: 她们通常是寡妇。

sentences.en: They have ceased to have children.
sentences.zh: 她们已经不再生育孩子了。

sentences.en: They're no longer fertile.
sentences.zh: 她们不再具有生育能力。

sentences.en: And those are really important things.
sentences.zh: 这些都是非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: And there are lots of reasons for why they're old, for why it's older women being attacked.
sentences.zh: 关于她们为什么年龄大、为什么是年长的女性遭受攻击，有很多原因。

sentences.en: But it's not just women.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是女性。

sentences.en: So, for example, particularly during the severe panics, 1611, for example, in Elwangen in Germany,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，特别是在严重的恐慌期间，例如1611年德国的埃尔万根，

sentences.en: there are 430 people who are executed as witches and they are men and women.
sentences.zh: 有430人作为女巫被处决，其中既有男性也有女性。

sentences.en: They include priests.
sentences.zh: 其中包括牧师。

sentences.en: They include a judge who's protested about his wife's arreSt.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一名因抗议妻子被捕而遭起诉的法官。

sentences.en: Sometimes witches, and this is a pretty terrible deviation, as it were, from the stereotype, are children.
sentences.zh: 有时女巫——这可以说是对刻板印象的一种相当可怕的偏离——是儿童。

sentences.en: So, again, in Germany, in the 1620s, in Würzburg, there are, I think it's more than 40 children who are executed as children.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样是在德国，在1620年代的维尔茨堡，我想有超过40名儿童被作为儿童处决。

sentences.en: That happens in the Basque country.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生在巴斯克地区。

sentences.en: Happens in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 发生在瑞典。

sentences.en: Have you seen the, a friend of mine made a film for Dispatches on Channel 4 about 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 你看过吗？我的一位朋友大约10年前为第四频道的《派遣》栏目制作过一部电影。

sentences.en: I think it's called Saving Africa's Witch Children.
sentences.zh: 我想这片子叫作《拯救非洲的巫童》。

sentences.en: I mean, we're massively moving forwards now, but this is, this is in southern Nigeria, where, of course, it's become a very radical form of Protestantism,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们现在取得了巨大的进步，但这是，这是在尼日利亚南部，在那里，这当然已经演变成了一种非常激进的基督新教形式，

sentences.en: but it's fused with local beliefs in spirits and demons.
sentences.zh: 但它与当地关于精灵和恶魔的信仰融合在了一起。

sentences.en: And there there's a whole kind of strain of evangelical Protestantism that says that, that witches are everywhere and that children are particularly prone to being witches
sentences.zh: 而且那里存在着一整支福音派新教流派，他们认为，巫师无处不在，儿童尤其容易成为巫师，

sentences.en: and children who get accused of it get kind of, at best, expelled from the family, at worst, tortured to death.
sentences.zh: 而被指控为巫师的孩子们，往好了说会被逐出家门，往坏了说会被折磨致死。

sentences.en: And I wondered, you know, is,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你知道的，这是否——

sentences.en: is that showing that we're talking about something that is universal and constant?
sentences.zh: 这是否表明我们讨论的是某种普遍且恒久的东西？

sentences.en: Or is it the fact that it's the Protestantism, it's the Christianity that is inspiring this?
sentences.zh: 还是说，这正是由于新教、由于基督教激发了这种现象？

sentences.en: Or what's going on there?
sentences.zh: 又或者那里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Can we kind of trace the patterns all the way through history, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为我们能否在整部历史中追溯出这种模式？

sentences.en: It's a difficult thing to answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难回答的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, it's certainly true that we have, there have been many witch hunts in recent times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可以肯定的是，我们经历过，近年来发生过很多次猎巫行动。

sentences.en: So in the late 80s, early 90s, there were 200 lynchings of suspected witches in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以在80年代末、90年代初，南非有200人因被怀疑是巫师而遭到私刑处决。

sentences.en: There have been,
sentences.zh: 还有，

sentences.en: there in 2001 in the Democratic Republic of Congo, there were unofficially, officially it's sort of figures around 800,
sentences.zh: 2001年在刚果民主共和国，非官方统计数字显示，官方数据大概是800人左右，

sentences.en: unofficially we're told it's more running into the thousands,
sentences.zh: 但非官方消息告诉我们，数字实际上达到了数千人，

sentences.en: witches killed, you know, murdered by lynching mobs, as it were.
sentences.zh: 被杀的巫师，你知道的，基本上就是惨死于私刑暴徒之手。

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia created an anti-witchcraft unit in 2009.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯在2009年成立了一个反巫术部队。

sentences.en: So, and we've seen it more recently, even, you know, wherever you look around the world,
sentences.zh: 所以，而且我们最近也看到了，甚至，你知道的，无论你环顾世界的哪个角落，

sentences.en: Nepal, Colombia, Indonesia, Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 尼泊尔、哥伦比亚、印度尼西亚、尼日利亚。

sentences.en: So it's a constant for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一个常态。

sentences.en: And I suppose even in Britain,
sentences.zh: 我想即使在英国，

sentences.en: I mean, Dominic, I don't know if you've researched the ritual satanic abuse scandals.
sentences.zh: 我是说，多米尼克，我不知道你有没有研究过关于仪式性撒旦虐待的丑闻。

sentences.en: Yeah, the 80s.
sentences.zh: 哦对，80年代的。

sentences.en: Cleveland, yeah.
sentences.zh: 克利夫兰，对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So was, in a sense, that's a kind of witchcraft scare, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，那也是一种猎巫恐慌，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I suppose you could probably argue that.
sentences.zh: 对，我想你大概可以这么说。

sentences.en: I mean, there's clearly, well, I don't know, maybe Susie would disagree with this, but I think there is a human constant, isn't there, to look for scapegoats.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，好吧，我不知道，也许苏西会不同意这一点，但我认为人类寻找替罪羊的倾向是一种常态，对吧？

sentences.en: And there are particular figures in society that end up being these folk devils.
sentences.zh: 社会中总有一些特定的人物最终会变成这种民间恶魔。

sentences.en: So older women, children, classically, and teenagers tend to be seen as folk devils,
sentences.zh: 所以老年女性、儿童，经典地，还有青少年，往往被视为民间恶魔，

sentences.en: generation after generation.
sentences.zh: 一代又一代人都是如此。

sentences.en: So maybe, disturbingly, there is this,
sentences.zh: 所以也许，令人不安的是，存在着这样一种——

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Susie, let me ask you a question, a slightly weird question.
sentences.zh: 苏西，我问你个问题，一个有点奇怪的问题。

sentences.en: If you were accused of being a witch, what's your best way of getting out of it?
sentences.zh: 如果你被指控为巫师，摆脱困境的最佳方法是什么？

sentences.en: So how would you escape?
sentences.zh: 那你该如何逃脱呢？

sentences.en: Let me just first come to that point about teenagers and older women.
sentences.zh: 让我先回到刚才关于青少年和老年女性的那一点。

sentences.en: I think perhaps the constant with children and teenagers and older women is that they're people that it's harder to control.
sentences.zh: 我想也许儿童、青少年和老年女性的共同点在于，他们是更难被控制的人。

sentences.en: I wonder if that's something to do with it.
sentences.zh: 我在想这是否与此有关。

sentences.en: How do you best escape?
sentences.zh: 如何才能最好地逃脱？

sentences.en: Actually, sometimes you can escape by confessing to it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时你可以通过供认来逃脱。

sentences.en: It depends where you are.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你在哪里。

sentences.en: So it depends on the jurisdiction you're operating in.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于你所处的司法管辖区。

sentences.en: In some places, people got away with it if they confessed and repented.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，如果人们承认并忏悔，就能逃过一劫。

sentences.en: That happened in Salem, in New England, and the trials in the 1692 outbreak.
sentences.zh: 塞勒姆就是这种情况，在英格兰新泽西，以及1692年爆发的审判中。

sentences.en: And it's those who refuse to confess that died quite often.
sentences.zh: 而且往往是那些拒绝认罪的人最终死去了。

sentences.en: But often actually by naming other people, that might be a way out of it.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，经常是通过供出其他人，这可能是一条出路。

sentences.en: That's kind of depressing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这听起来挺令人沮丧的，不是吗？

sentences.en: But it's like Russia in the 1930s or something.
sentences.zh: 但这就像30年代的俄罗斯什么的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: So if you can name people who were in large numbers who were there at your sabbat or whatever they've come up with as an idea, because quite often it's the interrogator's ideas
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能说出大量的人名，说他们曾在你的夜宴或其他他们凭空捏造的想法中出现过，因为这往往是审讯者的想法，

sentences.en: that are being reproduced by those who are being interrogated, then maybe you've got a chance of being let off.
sentences.zh: 被审讯者只是在重复这些想法，那么你或许还有机会被放过。

sentences.en: And was the ducking stool, was that a real thing or is that a kind of children's history book invention?
sentences.zh: 那么那个浸水椅，那是真实存在的还是某种儿童历史书里虚构出来的东西？

sentences.en: It's a real thing, but not for witches.
sentences.zh: 那是真实存在的，但不是用来对付巫师的。

sentences.en: It's a real thing that's used for scolds.
sentences.zh: 那是用来惩罚长舌妇的真实工具。

sentences.en: So in exactly the same period that we have a rise in the number of people being executed as witches, we see basically there's a great, there's a sort of, how do we put it,
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们看到因被指控为巫师而被处决的人数激增的同一时期，我们基本上看到了一种巨大的，有一种，我们该怎么说呢，

sentences.en: intensification of patriarchy in this period of time.
sentences.zh: 这一时期父权制的强化。

sentences.en: And so women who speak out, who are, you know, cantankerous or who are gossips or these sort of things can be ducked as scolds.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些直言不讳、脾气暴躁、爱说闲话或诸如此类的女性会被绑在浸水椅上惩罚。

sentences.en: But it's basically, it's just a confusion.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，这只是一种混淆。

sentences.en: What we do have is what's called swimming, which is in England,
sentences.zh: 我们真正拥有的是所谓的“水刑测试”（swimming），在英格兰，

sentences.en: our swam,
sentences.zh: 我们把它叫做浸水，

sentences.en: which is something that James I writes about in his demonology, which is the following.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯一世在他的《妖术学》中写到了这一点，具体是这样的。

sentences.en: You've got your witch, male or female, you strip them naked, you tie their thumbs to their toes and you put them in a river to see if they're going to,
sentences.zh: 你抓到一个巫师，无论男女，扒光他们的衣服，把他们的拇指和脚趾绑在一起，然后把他们扔进河里，看他们会不会——

sentences.en: sorry, that's the dog, you put them in a river to see if they're going to sink.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，那是我的狗，把他们扔进河里看他们会不会下沉。

sentences.en: Your familiar.
sentences.zh: 你的魔宠。

sentences.en: Yeah, my familiars are nearby.
sentences.zh: 对，我的魔宠就在附近。

sentences.en: So you, if they are innocent, they will sink and, you know, you hope they're going to be pulled out in time to not drown.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们是无辜的，他们就会下沉，然后，你知道的，你希望他们能及时被捞上来以免溺水。

sentences.en: And if they float, they are a witch.
sentences.zh: 如果他们浮在水面上，他们就是巫师。

sentences.en: And the logic is that their baptism,
sentences.zh: 其逻辑是，他们的洗礼，

sentences.en: their baptism
sentences.zh: 他们的洗礼

sentences.en: in waters no longer
sentences.zh: 在水中不再

sentences.en: holds because they have turned to the devil and so the waters will reject them.
sentences.zh: 奏效，因为他们已经转向了魔鬼，所以水会排斥他们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So on that thing of rejecting your baptism and you become a worshipper of the devil, this idea that you are leaving the Christian faith and that you were, in a sense,
sentences.zh: 所以在拒绝洗礼并成为魔鬼崇拜者这一点上，这种你正在背离基督教信仰、并且在某种意义上，

sentences.en: are taking up another faith.
sentences.zh: 正在接受另一种信仰的观点，

sentences.en: There was a very popular theory
sentences.zh: 曾有一个非常流行的理论，

sentences.en: that this was an expression of a kind of ancient paganism that had survived Christianity.
sentences.zh: 认为这是某种在基督教中幸存下来的古代异教的表象。

sentences.en: And I always remember my parents, when I was a child, had a book of kind of gazetteer to folklore and they had a wonderful thing about the death of William II in the New Forest
sentences.zh: 我总是记得我父母在我小时候有一本民间传说地名辞典，里面有一段关于威廉二世在新森林死亡的精彩记载，

sentences.en: and this, he'd been shot by an arrow and this supposedly was part of a satanic ritual.
sentences.zh: 据说他是被一支箭射死的，而这据称是撒旦仪式的一部分。

sentences.en: Kind of wicker man style.
sentences.zh: 有点像《异教徒》（The Wicker Man）那样的风格。

sentences.en: A wicker man, yes, which I'd always, which I'd always wanted to,
sentences.zh: 《异教徒》，是的，我一直，我一直想去——

sentences.en: I'd always wanted to believe.
sentences.zh: 我一直都愿意相信这一点。

sentences.en: But Susie, it's not true, is it?
sentences.zh: 但苏西，这不是真的，对吧？

sentences.en: There was no such
sentences.zh: 根本没有什么

sentences.en: pagan cult lasting into the early modern period that witches were belonging to.
sentences.zh: 持续到近代早期的异教崇拜是巫师们所归属的。

sentences.en: Well, I can say with great certainty there's no evidence to prove it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可以非常肯定地说，没有证据证明这一点。

sentences.en: I can't say it's not true but I can say
sentences.zh: 我不能说这不是真的，但我可以指出

sentences.en: there's perilous little to make the case for it.
sentences.zh: 支持这一说法的证据少得可怜。

sentences.en: But Susie, that then raises the question,
sentences.zh: 但苏西，这就引发了一个问题，

sentences.en: were there, so were any of the witches actually guilty?
sentences.zh: 那么，有没有任何巫师实际上是有罪的？

sentences.en: i.e., were any of the cases kind of banged to rights?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，是否有任何案件是证据确凿的？

sentences.en: They actually had been consorting, I mean, obviously they hadn't been consorting with the devil, but did they think they were witches?
sentences.zh: 她们真的曾与魔鬼勾结——当然，显然她们没有与魔鬼勾结，但她们是否认为自己是巫师？

sentences.en: i.e., had they been doing spells and did they have a, you know, a familiar and all this sort of business?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，她们是否施过法术，是否拥有你知道的魔宠以及所有这些乱七八糟的东西？

sentences.en: Well, this is the amazing thing about the witchcraft trials is exactly this question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于巫术审判，最神奇的就是这个问题。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: many of us looking at this see this as one historian described it as a, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们许多人看到这一点，正如一位历史学家所描述的那样，它是一个，你知道的，

sentences.en: a crime with a hole at the centre of it.
sentences.zh: 一个中心空洞的罪行。

sentences.en: There is, you know, there is nothing there
sentences.zh: 那里，你知道的，什么都没有，

sentences.en: and they're not doing anything, but clearly some of these people did think that they were acting as witches.
sentences.zh: 她们什么也没做，但显然其中一些人确实认为自己在扮演巫师的角色。

sentences.en: At least that's what the, that's what the confessions seem to suggeSt.
sentences.zh: 至少，忏悔似乎是这么暗示的。

sentences.en: Now, obviously there are lots of confessions that are extracted under torture, but then there are also confessions that are freely given and some of those do seem to suggest that,
sentences.zh: 当然，有很多供词是在酷刑下逼出来的，但也有一些供词是自愿给出的，其中一些似乎确实表明，

sentences.en: and we can psychologise about what's going on there, but some of them do seem to suggest that people are saying they've met with the devil.
sentences.zh: 我们可以对那里发生的事情进行心理分析，但其中一些确实似乎表明人们在说他们曾与魔鬼会面。

sentences.en: And some of the interesting work, again, actually from
sentences.zh: 一些有趣的研究，同样来自

sentences.en: Linda Roper
sentences.zh: 琳达·罗珀（Linda Roper），

sentences.en: has looked at the idea that what we're seeing is their fantasies that quite a lot of the time these are people who are poor and dispossessed and who have very little
sentences.zh: 她研究了这样一种观点：我们所看到的其实是他们的幻想，很多时候，这些人都是贫穷和被剥夺权利的人，几乎一无所有，

sentences.en: and they fantasise about meeting with the devil and him, you know, freeing them from hunger and from want and from poverty and, you know, lots of feasting goes on with the devil.
sentences.zh: 他们幻想与魔鬼会面，幻想魔鬼，你知道的，将他们从饥饿、匮乏和贫困中解放出来，你知道的，他们会和魔鬼一起享受饕餮盛宴。
